elements.element: The transition and data-return obligations apply upon expiration or termination of the agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 expressly begins, “Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason,” and survives expiration or termination.

elements.element: Commerce One must provide transition assistance to Corio following expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: Commerce One is required to provide assistance only “at Corio’s request.” The preferred position does not make the post-termination assistance obligation conditional on a separate request.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for up to six months.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4(i) provides assistance “for a period of up to six (6) months.”

elements.element: Transition assistance must be provided at Commerce One’s then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4(i) expressly uses “Commerce One’s then-current rates.”

elements.element: Commerce One must return or deliver Customer Data to Corio following expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4(ii) covers all data of Corio, its Customers, and Software Users in Commerce One’s possession or control, but return or export is conditioned on Corio making a request.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned within 30 days after expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: The 30-day period runs from “Corio’s request,” not from expiration or termination. If Corio requests the data later, the operative language permits delivery more than 30 days after the agreement ends.

elements.element: Customer Data must be returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4(ii) requires a “commonly used, machine-readable format,” satisfying the standard machine-readable format requirement.

elements.element: Commerce One must delete Customer Data after returning or exporting it.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4(iii) requires Commerce One to “thereafter delete such data from its systems.”

elements.element: Commerce One must certify deletion of Customer Data after deletion.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4(iii) requires Commerce One to “certify such deletion to Corio in writing.”

elements.element: The transition-assistance and data-export obligations apply upon expiration or termination of the agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 11.4 expressly applies upon expiration or termination for any reason and states that it survives those events.

elements.element: Commerce One must provide transition assistance to Corio following expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: The assistance obligation is conditioned on a request from Corio rather than arising without the additional request condition.

elements.element: Transition assistance must be available for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: The clause makes assistance available for up to six months, which encompasses a 90-day assistance period.

elements.element: Commerce One must export Customer Data to Corio following expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: The clause permits return or export to Corio, but only after Corio requests it; the fallback does not state this additional condition.

elements.element: Customer Data must be exported within 30 days after expiration or termination.
elements.evidence: The deadline is 30 days after Corio’s request, so the export may occur more than 30 days after expiration or termination.

result.reason: The added section is targeted to transition assistance, data return, and deletion and leaves the existing survival and support terms intact. It includes the preferred six-month period, then-current rates, machine-readable format, deletion, and written certification. However, both assistance and data return/export are conditioned on Corio’s request, and—most importantly—the 30-day data deadline runs from that request rather than from expiration or termination. Because those additional triggers can delay or prevent performance, neither the preferred nor fallback position is fully satisfied. Drafting is otherwise clear, but the request-based timing materially departs from the stated rule.
